dedupe_keys.name: ncdr disaster prevention data service platform and 3d disaster potential map taiwan

description: The National Science and Technology Center for Disaster Reduction (NCDR) of Taiwan runs two public services that together make its hazard data available. The disaster prevention data service platform is a catalogue of disaster prevention and relief data, with advanced search, data categories, newly listed and popular datasets, open data and datasets on application, open and applied API services, and example applications such as climate change disaster risk maps for government and industry, disaster response map cards, high and low temperature warnings and flash flood and lowland flooding early warning. The 3D disaster potential map shows where disasters have happened or are more likely, by theme: flood potential, landslides and debris flows, faults and soil liquefaction, coastal hazards, tsunami inundation and volcanic hazards, with settlement environment views for slopes, flooding and coasts, warning threshold queries and map data downloads. Access to open data and the map is free online; some data and API services need an application and login, and the map site asks users to cite NCDR, with no licence named on the pages read. Caveats: the pages are in Chinese, and a notice of 3 September 2026 says the map stopped overlaying external layers for security reasons. Coverage is Taiwan. It supports hazard exposure and emergency response analysis for roads, settlements, utilities and other infrastructure facing floods, landslides, earthquakes and tsunamis; related records are the NIED bosaiXview maps and the Mexico Atlas Nacional de Riesgos.
